en.headline: Very Hot Weather Warning remains in force as temperatures stay elevated
en.dek: The Hong Kong Observatory continues the warning issued on Sunday, forecasting sunny periods and a maximum of around 33°C on Monday before heavier showers and thunderstorms develop later.
body: The Hong Kong Observatory said the Very Hot Weather Warning remained in force early Monday after being issued at 6.45 a.m. on Sunday. At 2 a.m. the temperature at the Observatory was 30 degrees Celsius with relative humidity at 85 per cent.

The forecast for Monday calls for becoming cloudy with a few showers, a minimum of about 28 degrees and a maximum around 33 degrees during sunny periods. Showers are expected to become heavier in some areas with squally thunderstorms later in the day as a broad trough of low pressure approaches.

The Observatory advised the public to beware of heat stroke, drink more water and avoid prolonged outdoor exposure during the hottest hours. Outdoor workers and those engaged in strenuous activity were urged to take extra precautions.

zh.headline: 酷熱天氣警告繼續生效 周一最高氣溫約33度
zh.dek: 天文台周日發出的酷熱天氣警告仍然生效，預料周一短暫陽光及酷熱，其後部分地區驟雨較大及有狂風雷暴。
body: 香港天文台表示，酷熱天氣警告繼續生效。該警告於周日上午6時45分發出。周一凌晨2時天文台氣溫為30度，相對濕度85%。
天文台預料周一漸轉多雲，有幾陣驟雨，最低氣溫約28度，日間部分時間有陽光及酷熱，最高氣溫約33度。稍後部分地區雨勢較大及有狂風雷暴。
天文台呼籲市民慎防中暑，多喝水，避免在最熱時段長時間在戶外逗留。戶外工作及進行劇烈活動人士應格外小心。
